content: isidentifier() is pretty cool but we're really relying on nobody knowing it in order for this to be a fun clash. To be honest, I think you should use a fictional identifier format so that it's more compatible with other languages and pushes people towards regex for shortest mode.

I think that all that you would need to do is include uppercase characters in the cases. You already state that a valid identifier can only contain lowercase letters, so that would be the easiest way to void isidentifier().

Edit: I was wrong. The solution would just become s.isidentifier() and s.islower()

Thanks for the suggestion! I've changed it to a fictional identifier format: lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, starting with a lowercase letter and ending with a lowercase letter or digit. For example, user-id is valid, while _user and user_ are invalid, so isidentifier() no longer matches the rules. I updated the tests and validators to cover these differences, uppercase letters, spaces and boundary lengths. All 8 tests and 8 validators pass in both Python and JavaScript.

Seems good. Just a couple more notes from me.
Validator 7 seems to differ too greatly from test 7.
The test cases and validators should have slightly different outputs where possible. I like the case pairing (aside from 7), so just changing the order of the strings for the validators would suffice.

Thanks! Validator 7 now uses a 100-character lowercase string, matching test 7. I also reordered the other validators so their outputs differ from the corresponding tests. All 8 tests and 8 validators pass.
